findings.title: Stray sed backup file committed
findings.description: A file named `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E` is in the tree. It is the usual byproduct of `sed -i -E` on macOS. It holds the pre-change copy of `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`, which still calls `createContextPipeline(path)` without the new required options argument. The name doesn't match `*.test.*`, so test runners won't pick it up. It is still dead duplicate content. It should be deleted, and `*-E` could be added to `.gitignore`.

findings.title: Magic default `'implementation'` duplicated in the integrator
findings.description: The new line `const instruction = project.instruction || 'implementation';` hard-codes a fallback instruction. It is computed before `mapProjectToEnhancedContext`, which presumably applies its own default for the same field. This breaks the project rules against magic defaults and against scattering comparison values. Neither the adoption eligibility check (`resolvePhaseValue(instruction)`) nor the mapping step should carry a private copy. Define the default once as a constant, or reuse the value the mapper already resolves. If the two defaults ever drift, adoption would be judged against an instruction different from the one that gets rendered.

findings.title: Required `adoptionStateWrites` option forces every caller to decide
findings.description: Making the option required means a caller can't forget it. I found three non-test callers (`build.ts:84`, `contextTools.ts:94`, and the `generateContext` wrapper). Each passes a value, and the tests assert `persist` for `cf build` and `context_build` and `read-only` for `template_preview`. In `generateContext`, the new positional `adoptionStateWrites` parameter sits before the optional ones. That is acceptable, but with 5+ positional parameters an options object would be more readable.

findings.title: Error handling and test coverage are sound
findings.description: `AdoptionError` is rethrown explicitly instead of falling back to an error stub, and a test covers this. `persistInProgress` wraps the write failure with `cause` and a remedy. The guide check runs before the state write, and a test asserts the state stays unset when the check fails. The `isSelected` switch uses an exhaustive `never` check. The tests cover selection, overrides, resume, shallow clones, monorepo subfolders, read-only previews, and CLI/MCP parity. No `any` was introduced.
